leaks_ranked.step: Claim page: landed -> gave email (the email gate)
leaks_ranked.rate: ~66% of claim visitors never type a key (43 of 65 sampled replays this window)
leaks_ranked.prior_rate: ~57% never type (40 of 70 sampled replays prior window)
leaks_ranked.why_real: Stable across both windows and corroborated by the prior [FACT] (~67% never type) and the 2026-07-20 cycle's larger replay sample (67%/69%). It is the largest single drop by headcount and GATES everything downstream (no email -> no code, no video, no in-app review ask). Honest caveat: the /session_recordings api caps at 100 rows/window so these are a directional SAMPLE not a census, and the PostHog query api that would give a frozen person-linked landed->email rate is 403, so no exact rate exists this cycle -- which is precisely why the 2026-07-20 diagnostic matters.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Highest of the three. Reviews come almost entirely from the in-app thank-you screen, which requires a created video, which requires an email (11/11 review clicks this window came from in_app thankyou). Each extra email is a fresh shot at ~46% email->video then ~39% video->review. Bounded, though: FUNNEL_CONTEXT guess #1 (a one-off gift buyer may not want a NEXT-order discount) would cap it, and we cannot yet separate that ceiling from a fixable cause.

leaks_ranked.step: In-app: gave email -> started a video (warm users promised a free video)
leaks_ranked.why_real: ~54% of already-warm users never start the video they were promised, consistent across windows. The nominal +10.6pts is NOT significant (p=0.22), so treat this as a persistent ~35-46% leak, not an improvement. Feeds reviews directly and the users are motivated.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Medium-high; directly upstream of every video and thus every in-app review ask. But the losing sub-step (arrived->role vs role->create) cannot be localised this cycle -- PostHog 403 and Supabase has no in-app 'arrived' event -- so a fix here would bet on an unverified cause, the exact failure that sank the last cycle.

leaks_ranked.step: Review ask on preview + share surfaces (video-preview.html / video.html)
leaks_ranked.rate: 0 review clicks from preview/share this window (all 11 came from in_app thankyou), against 28 preview_opened
leaks_ranked.prior_rate: 2 review clicks from preview (video_preview_receiver) prior window, against 34 preview_opened
leaks_ranked.why_real: Consistently ~0 despite real preview traffic; attacked once in June (non-destructive post-share highlight) with no effect; ANALYTICS.md notes the review ask sits BELOW the share button. Stable behaviour.
leaks_ranked.size_of_prize: Low. It is a redundant SECOND review ask -- the buyer already met a better-placed ask on the in-app thank-you screen (which harvests essentially all review intent), so the second ask converts almost nobody. Biggest percentage loss but lowest value to reviews: ranked by value, not by percentage. (Also note: adding a review link to the video-ready EMAIL was owner-rejected 2026-07-21, so the adjacent email surface is closed too.)

biggest_leak: The claim-page email gate is the biggest and most review-critical leak, so I am attacking it -- but this cycle by REPAIRING the diagnostic instrument that will tell us WHY people leave, rather than piling a blind conversion change onto ground that is spent for presentation (PR #8) and closed to the code-first move (owner-rejected), and rather than betting on an unverified cause the way the last cycle did.

choice_reasoning.expected_value_to_reviews: Indirect but the highest available. The claim gate produces every video and thus (via the in-app thank-you) essentially every review. We cannot yet separate 'never intended to give an email' (a hard ceiling) from 'engaged the field and gave up' (fixable) -- and the only instrument that can, email_field_engaged (shipped 2026-07-20, first readable ~2026-08-03), is currently undercounting. Repairing it now, two weeks before its first read, is what lets the NEXT cycle aim a real fix at a verified cause. A corrupted 08-03 read would waste a full month of accumulation.
choice_reasoning.already_tried_here: Coverage map: claim landed->email has 1 real conversion attempt (PR #8 layout/hierarchy rebuild -> flat 44.5%->39.0%), one owner-rejected proposal (code-first), and one measurement-only ship (2026-07-20 instrumentation). Presentation reshuffles are explicitly spent; code-first is explicitly rejected. What is NOT spent is making the leak diagnosable -- 2026-07-20 started that and this change finishes it correctly.
choice_reasoning.what_history_suggests: Pattern across all changes: the one durable WIN (2026-06-16) changed a MECHANISM (email-first delivery) on a warm-user step; the one FLAT attempt (PR #8) was a claim-page presentation reshuffle; the message-step copy tweak is unprovable at this traffic. So mechanism changes on the right step move this funnel, presentation reshuffles do not -- and nothing moves without a correct measurement to read it. That argues: fix measurement here first, then make a mechanism (not presentation) bet next cycle once the cause is visible.
choice_reasoning.why_not_the_others: Leak 2 (email->video) is high value but its losing sub-step cannot be localised this cycle (PostHog 403, no Supabase in-app 'arrived' event) -- a fix would bet on an unverified cause. Leak 3 (preview/share review ask) is the biggest percentage but the lowest EV: a redundant second ask after the in-app thank-you already harvests review intent, already attacked once with no effect, and the adjacent email surface was just owner-rejected.

diagnosis.question: Why do ~66% of claim visitors never enter an email -- and, prerequisite to answering it, is the instrument we built to answer it (email_field_engaged + per-visitor visitor_id) actually recording faithfully?
hypotheses_considered: H1 Never intended to give an email (discount is for a NEXT order; one-off gift buyer) -- a ceiling, not a fixable leak.
H2 Engaged the field and gave up (form friction / hesitation) -- fixable.
H3 Never reached/engaged the field (distracted, satisfied by the autoplay video, left) -- different fix.
H4 The email_field_engaged instrument is itself undercounting, so the 08-03 sub-funnel meant to separate H1/H2/H3 will be wrong.
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: Parsed PostHog session-recording metadata for every claim.html recording the api returned in both frozen windows (65 this window, 70 prior; api caps at 100/window so this is a sample). Never-typed share is stable (66% vs 57%) and corroborates the prior ~67% [FACT]. Bounce timing contradicts an early-exit/legibility cause: only 12 of 43 non-typers this window leave in <5s active; the median non-typer is active ~8s (max 36s) -- they see the page and decline, not instantly bounce (the same over-claim the last cycle made about a '2s blur'). Then, on the instrument: in the 07-20..07-22 deploy window email_field_engaged fired 4 times vs email_entered 6 -- impossible for a true superset. Grouping the raw claim rows by visitor_id showed 4 clean chains plus a submitter with NEITHER a field_engaged event NOR a visitor_id.
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: Two concrete, code-level defects in the 2026-07-20 diagnostic: (a) the field-engagement listener is bound to 'focus' only (claim.html:1561), so autofill/paste submissions (common on mobile with saved emails) submit without ever firing it -> email_field_engaged is not the superset of email_entered it must be; (b) getVisitorId() returns null when sessionStorage is blocked (private mode / messaging-app in-app browsers, a large share of QR traffic; claim.html:1175-1178), so those sessions' three claim events are unlinkable and drop out of the visitor_id sub-funnels. Both directly corrupt the page_viewed->email_field_engaged->email_entered read due ~2026-08-03.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: It still cannot tell H1 (never intended) from H2 (engaged and declined) -- that is exactly what the REPAIRED instrument will measure at the 08-03 read. It also cannot confirm what the non-typers' clicks land on (the autoplay video preview is the leading guess but replay metadata gives click COUNTS, not targets), and the recording sample is capped at 100/window so replay-derived rates are directional, not exact.

plan.title: Harden the claim-page email-gate diagnostic so its 2026-08-03 read is trustworthy (capture autofill/paste engagement + keep sessions linkable when storage is blocked)
plan.targets: Claim page: landed -> gave email (its diagnostic instrumentation -- email_field_engaged and visitor_id linking added 2026-07-20)
plan.mechanism: Two surgical instrument fixes, no user-facing/UI change. (1) Fire email_field_engaged on the email input's 'input' event in ADDITION to 'focus', guarded by a shared once-flag so it still fires at most once per visit. 'input' fires on autofill, paste, and first keystroke, so field-engagement becomes a true superset of email_entered instead of missing autofill/paste submitters. (2) When sessionStorage is unavailable, getVisitorId() falls back to a module-scoped in-memory UUID (kept for the page's lifetime) instead of returning null -- all three claim events fire within a single page load, so an in-memory id keeps them linkable per person even in private/in-app browsers. Also fix a stale tooling bug: add email_field_engaged to the ordered event list in tools/funnel-report.mjs (line 86) so it stops being falsely flagged '(non-canonical!)'.
plan.assumed_cause: The email_field_engaged / visitor_id instrument shipped 2026-07-20 is undercounting (focus-only listener misses autofill/paste; null visitor_id when storage is blocked), so without repair the 2026-08-03 sub-funnel read meant to separate 'never engaged the field' from 'engaged and declined' will be wrong.

cause_verification.for: In the exact 07-20..07-22 deploy window, funnel-report shows email_field_engaged=4 but email_entered=6 -- a strict impossibility if the event were the intended superset, since you must engage the field to submit. Grouping the raw phase=claim rows by properties.visitor_id shows 4 perfect chains AND one submitter bucket with no field_engaged event and visitor_id='(none)'. The listener source (claim.html:1561) is bound only to 'focus'; getVisitorId (claim.html:1175-1178) returns null on a sessionStorage exception. These are code facts, not statistical inferences.
cause_verification.against: I actively searched for innocent explanations that would make a fix unnecessary. (i) Small-N noise -- could 4<6 just be luck over 2 days? Checked the per-visitor rows, not just aggregate counts: the miss is a REAL submitter with a missing event, and the null-visitor_id bucket is a distinct real failure, not a counting fluke. (ii) Network drop of the keepalive POST -- both field_engaged and email_entered use identical keepalive POSTs to /api/track, so random drops would hit email_entered equally and would not concentrate in the storage-blocked/(none) session, but the miss DOES concentrate there, pointing to focus/storage mechanics not the network. (iii) Listener attaching too late -- getElementById succeeds at script run and the field is only revealed after the popup, so focus cannot precede the listener; ruled out. Residual uncertainty is only the PREVALENCE of autofill vs blocked-storage (N=6 cannot size it), and the fixes are correct for either mix with no downside if a session had neither problem.
cause_verification.why_for_wins: The 'for' is a code-level certainty (a focus-only listener cannot observe an autofill; a null id cannot be linked) that the data corroborates. Even at small prevalence today, an uncorrected instrument yields a fatally misleading 08-03 read -- email_field_engaged->email_entered would exceed 100% and 'never engaged' would be overstated -- which would send the next cycle after a phantom cause. The fix is cheap, reversible, and strictly increases the fidelity of the one measurement the biggest leak depends on.

plan.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: This ships against a MEASUREMENT step, not an exchange step, so there is no user 'price' being paid -- the change alters nothing the visitor sees, gives, or gets. It exists so the email-gate exchange (the discount+video is the price of the email) can be diagnosed honestly before anyone tries to reprice it.
what_would_have_to_be_true: 'input' reliably fires on autofill and paste in the mobile browsers/in-app webviews QR traffic uses (it does per the DOM spec and is the standard autofill-detection hook).

All three claim events (page_viewed, email_field_engaged, email_entered) fire within a single page load, so an in-memory fallback id links them (true -- the claim page is a single-page flow with no reload between them).
The once-guard prevents double counting when both 'focus' and 'input' fire on the same visit (a shared boolean flag).
plan.second_order_effects: email_field_engaged counts will rise once autofill/paste sessions are captured, and visitor_id-null rows will drop -- so 08-03 numbers are NOT comparable to any pre-fix baseline for this event; I will state the discontinuity in the changelog and treat pre-fix rows as lower bounds. No conversion event changes: email_entered, video_started, review_clicked and their cross-app linking (which key on email/operation_id, not visitor_id) are untouched, so no verdict funnel is disturbed. The in-memory id is per page load so it never over-links across visits. One step further: making the biggest-leak diagnostic trustworthy is what enables next cycle to choose a MECHANISM fix (the kind history says moves this funnel) instead of a presentation reshuffle (the kind that went flat).
plan.strongest_case_against: A sharp sceptic says: this is the THIRD consecutive measurement-only cycle (07-16, 07-20, now) on a project whose owner keeps listing CONVERSION as the target -- you are polishing instruments while the funnel sits still, and 4-vs-6 over two days is too thin to justify touching anything. Honest answer: the defect is a code certainty, not a statistical claim -- a focus-only listener demonstrably cannot see an autofill and a null id demonstrably cannot be linked -- and the cost of NOT fixing it is concrete and time-boxed: the 08-03 read (the entire payoff of last cycle) would be corrupted and we would lose another month. Every conversion alternative this cycle requires betting on a cause I cannot verify (PostHog 403; no in-app replays), the exact unverified-cause mistake the last cycle was faulted for. Given a two-week clock to the read, repairing the instrument now is the highest-integrity, highest-EV move; and I am explicitly NOT hiding behind it -- the plan commits the next cycle to a mechanism-level conversion bet driven by the repaired read.
plan.expected_effect: No conversion effect (and none claimed). Effect is measurement fidelity: email_field_engaged becomes a true superset of email_entered, and storage-blocked sessions become person-linkable, so page_viewed->email_field_engaged and email_field_engaged->email_entered are computable and correct at the 2026-08-03 read.

tradeoff.gained: A trustworthy first read (~2026-08-03) of WHERE the biggest, most review-critical leak actually leaks -- never-engaged vs engaged-and-declined -- the prerequisite to any real fix and thus to more videos and more reviews.
tradeoff.risked: Opportunity cost of a cycle spent on measurement rather than a conversion experiment. Quantified downside to live conversion is ~0 (no user-facing change; conversion logging and cross-app linking untouched). The only numeric risk is analytic: email_field_engaged counts are discontinuous across the fix, so pre-fix rows must be treated as lower bounds -- flagged in the changelog. Downstream review-reminder path is unaffected: email_redirect review clicks were 0 this window / 2 prior, and this change touches neither email capture nor Klaviyo.
unverified_assumptions: OWNER QUESTION / FACT CORRECTION to raise, not resolve: FUNNEL_CONTEXT states as [FACT] that the QR link carries ONLY ?sku (no code, no source) and that codes are unique/single-use with 'no shared code to print'. But session-recording start_urls show ~83% of claim traffic now arriving with code=GOTYOU30 and source=insert|box, and claim.html reads params.get('code') into state.discountCode and passes it to Klaviyo as the profile attribute discount_code (klaviyo-subscribe.js:76). Is GOTYOU30 a real, redeemable, MULTI-USE 30% code now printed on the insert cards? If yes, a documented premise of the email gate is weaker than recorded. NOTE: showing a code up front remains owner-rejected, so this is a FACT to correct and a strategic question for the owner -- NOT a lever this plan pulls.
Whether the instrument miss is mostly autofill vs blocked-storage (N=6 cannot size it); the fix is correct for either and harmless if neither applies to a given session.

OWNER QUESTION (carried from 2026-07-20, still blocking): can the PostHog personal API key be regranted the query:read scope? Without it the whole claim top-of-funnel is measurable only once the durable events accumulate -- the single biggest measurement blocker.

plan.differs_from_past_attempt: NOT PR #8 (a claim-page layout/hierarchy REDESIGN for capture -> flat; this ships ZERO presentation/UI change). NOT the owner-rejected code-first move (this shows and gives away nothing; the email exchange is untouched). NOT the owner-rejected review-link-in-video-email (this touches no email surface). It REPAIRS two defects in the 2026-07-20 instrument (focus-only listener; null visitor_id) that its own 'verified live' synthetic test could not surface because synthetic POSTs neither autofill nor run in a storage-blocked webview -- the prior auditor forced the visitor_id fix but could not have caught these. It also does not repeat the last cycle's error of aiming a fix at an unverified early-exit cause; here the cause is a code certainty and the change is measurement-only.
plan.how_to_verify: Boot locally (PORT=3939 node --experimental-websocket server.js), load claim.html?sku=PTT-GREEN1&code=GOTYOU30&source=insert. (1) Autofill/paste the email WITHOUT clicking the field first -> confirm one email_field_engaged POST fires (Network tab / a synthetic /api/track row). (2) Focus then type -> confirm still exactly ONE email_field_engaged (once-guard holds). (3) Disable sessionStorage (simulate private mode) and complete page_viewed+field_engaged+email_entered -> confirm all three share a non-null visitor_id and linked-funnel --link-by=visitor_id returns them as one person. (4) Run funnel-report and confirm email_field_engaged no longer prints '(non-canonical!)'. Delete all synthetic rows by id afterward. Then at ~2026-08-03: run the two --link-by=visitor_id sub-funnels from the 2026-07-20 entry and significance-test each.
alternatives_rejected: Ship a claim-page conversion change now: blocked -- presentation is spent (PR #8), code-first is rejected, and any other cause is unverifiable this cycle (PostHog 403, no in-app replays), so it would be a blind bet of the exact kind that sank the last cycle.
Attack email->video (leak 2): can't localise the losing sub-step this cycle (no in-app 'arrived' event in Supabase, PostHog 403) -> unverified cause.

Attack the preview/share review ask (leak 3): lowest EV (redundant second ask after the in-app thank-you), already attacked once with no effect, and the adjacent email surface was just owner-rejected.
Do nothing / wait for 08-03: rejected because the read it waits on would itself be corrupted by these defects -- fixing them now is what makes the wait worthwhile.
Force localStorage to fix null-visitor_id at the source: rejected -- storage may be fully blocked and it adds a persistence/consent surface; an in-memory fallback is the minimal robust fix.
